outlet.jets: Horizontal, one each side of the nozzle as in revision 41: the slot under the duct-to-slot wall (|X| 10.2), from the floor to the wall's flat bottom (Z-73.6, unchanged). The floor is 0.4 mm lower from Y19.0 forward (Z-77.05000000000001 where flat, was -76.65; the same 0.4 mm lower where it climbs the heel), out to |X| 12.85, rising at 45 degrees into the front wall; it is still solid, so no air blows down at the bed. The wall's duct side is rounded r 2.4 (was 1.4) from Y16.69 to Y26.2, on a foot out to |X| 12.6 with a 45 degree chamfer above, narrowing at 45 degrees in plan behind Y17.6.
outlet.note: Open area in planes across the jets (|X| 10.3-11.5), inside P22's outer profile. Floor thickness by vertical rays on the exact solid (0.8 mm by design: two perimeters) and by ray cast along the surface normal on the printed mesh. The bell-mouth band is measured by its profile against the design (thickness across X at heights over ROOF, both sides), and the rest of the outlet against revision 41's, less the same bands.

hotends.note: Exact distances (cutoff 8 mm). The carriage backs 60 mm away in -Y in 0.5 mm steps with the tool left in its dock, as in the requalification; every smallest gap is at the mounted position.

fit.note: Gap 0 with no overlap is face contact (P22 seated on P23, the screws in their holes). 'p22_over_p23_top': P22's area in the 0.01 mm over P23's top face, where P23 bears on it.

print.still_needs_support: The cheeks' bearing faces, where P22 seats on P01's bosses: in print, ceilings 8.5 mm wide cantilevered 10 mm from the duct, over P22 itself, so the support stands on P22's top. And the undersides of the two 6.1 mm bosses that locate P23's rear ears, which stand 2.2 mm proud and print lying on their side (the area a support from the plate can reach): they would print unsupported, but they fit P23's sockets with 0.10 mm of radial clearance, so a droop would make the ears tight.
print.bridges: The socket's front lip (15.4 mm), the skin under the window notch (22.9 mm long, 1.8 mm wide), the jets' front lips (3.7 mm); the cable boss's nose inside the duct is a 7 mm arch.
print.note: Facets facing down more steeply than the preset's 30 degree threshold, split by whether a support from the plate can reach them. With P22 on its back face, revision 43's new faces stand vertical or face up, or overhang at 45 degrees (the window notch, the back chamfer, the floor's front chamfers and the bell-mouth foot's back ends); the ends of the larger round at the jet's heel overhang by less than 0.5 mm. The sweep stands P22 on each of its flat faces with 50 mm2 or more on the plate.

frame_source.note: Nominal frame, panels and door from 01_Voron24_350_Frame_and_Enclosure as world bounding boxes (conservative for the extrusion profiles). No Z drives, bed supports or bed wiring are modeled.

hardware: Unchanged: P22's inserts, the P22-to-P01 button heads and the probe screws stay as in revisions 41 and 42.
limitations: Rigid CAD and sampled straight paths. Airflow is simulated separately (cfd_cpap_r43.py, verification_cfd_cpap_r43.json), not measured.
The Bambu hotend and its silicone sock are this project's model of the P2S hotend; a real sock up to the margins in 'hotends' still clears. Measure yours if it differs.
The floor under the jets is 0.8 mm, two perimeters with P22 on its back face, under the 1.0 mm minimum used elsewhere on the CPAP parts; it carries no load, and the jets keep it cool.

Printability is judged on the meshes (overhang angle, rays to the plate), not on a print: the cheeks' bearing faces and the undersides of P23's two locating bosses still need support, and the bridges listed under 'print' are left to the slicer.
